rules.title: match must be exhaustive
rules.statement: A `match` over a scrutinee of type T must cover every value of T. If a reachable value is uncovered the program is rejected (e.g. enum: 'match is not exhaustive — missing variant(s): ...'; bool: 'match on bool is not exhaustive — missing true/false').

rules.title: match on uninhabited scrutinee is exhaustive
rules.statement: A match whose scrutinee type is uninhabited — the `Never` type, or an enum with zero variants — is trivially exhaustive and requires no arms; a bare `match x {}` is accepted.

rules.title: unguarded wildcard arm makes match exhaustive
rules.statement: An arm whose pattern is an unguarded wildcard `_` covers all remaining values, making the match exhaustive regardless of which enum variants or bool values are otherwise matched.

rules.title: guarded arms do not contribute to exhaustiveness
rules.statement: An arm carrying a guard (`if <cond>`) is not counted toward exhaustiveness coverage; only unguarded arms cover variants/values, since a guard may fail at runtime.

rules.title: enum match coverage by variant
rules.statement: For an enum scrutinee, an unguarded `Variant` or `VariantData` pattern covers that variant (identified by discriminant); an or-pattern covers the union of its alternatives. A match without a wildcard is exhaustive iff every (constructable) variant is covered.

rules.title: variant with uninhabited payload may be omitted
rules.statement: An enum variant whose payload (after substituting the scrutinee's type arguments into the enum's type parameters) contains an uninhabited type can never be constructed and need not have an arm; its omission does not break exhaustiveness.
examples: match r: Result<i32, Void> { Ok(x) => x }  // Err arm omittable when Void is empty

rules.title: redundant wildcard arm over fully-covered unit enum
rules.statement: A wildcard arm is reported unreachable ('unreachable wildcard arm: every variant of the enum is already covered explicitly') when the enum is non-empty, all its variants are unit (payload-free), and every variant is explicitly covered. For payload-bearing variants the warning is suppressed (disc-only coverage cannot distinguish refutable inner patterns).

rules.title: bool match must cover true and false
rules.statement: A match on a `bool` scrutinee without a wildcard arm must include unguarded `true` and `false` patterns; otherwise it is rejected as non-exhaustive.

rules.title: match consumes scrutinee when an arm moves out a value
rules.statement: Matching a by-value (move-type) scrutinee whose arm binds out a value by name marks the scrutinee place moved. This applies to: whole-value bindings, struct destructures that bind a move-only field by value, tuple destructures that bind a move-only element by value, and variant-data arms that bind a move-only payload by value. `_` bindings and `ref` bindings move nothing and leave the scrutinee live.

rules.title: ref bindings and _ borrow/discard rather than move
rules.statement: A `ref`-bound binding borrows its place and a `_` (anonymous wildcard) discards it; neither consumes the matched value, recursively through nested tuple and struct sub-patterns. A by-value name binding (including struct-field shorthand `{ name }`) consumes the value.

rules.title: bare variant names resolve via prelude/alias remap
rules.statement: A variant pattern written with only a variant name (no enum qualifier) resolves its enum: `Some`/`None` → `Option`, `Ok`/`Err` → `Result`, and otherwise via the importing module's variant aliases.

rules.title: pattern matching peels references
rules.statement: When checking exhaustiveness against a scrutinee type, reference and pointer layers (`&T`, `&mut T`, `*T`) are peeled (up to a fixed depth) to the underlying type before variant analysis; matching `&E` covers `E`'s variants.

rules.title: exhaustiveness recurses into single-field variant payloads
rules.statement: A variant covered only by a refutable single-field payload pattern is treated as covered iff the inner patterns collectively exhaust the (substituted) payload type; an all-wildcard payload, an empty payload-arg list, or a bare `Variant` pattern covers the variant fully.

rules.title: or-patterns flatten and @-bindings unwrap for coverage
rules.statement: For exhaustiveness, or-patterns (`p1 | p2`) are flattened to their alternatives and `@`-bindings (`name @ p`) are unwrapped to their inner sub-pattern.
